questions.prompt: Which of the following helped spread the Great Depression around the world?
choices: The opening of new markets in Asia
Falling tariffs that expanded world trade
Rising tariffs that shrank world trade
The end of all trade in 1929
questions.explanation: Countries raised tariffs, and trade shrank, spreading the crisis.
choiceExplanations: Countries raised tariffs, and trade shrank, spreading the crisis.
Trade shrank but did not end.
questions.distinguisher: Tariffs rose, not fell, during the Depression.

questions.prompt: The New Deal differed from Stalin's Five-Year Plans in that the New Deal
choices: put the entire economy under state control
forced peasants onto collective farms
abolished private banks in the United States
kept private property and markets
questions.explanation: The New Deal regulated but preserved private property and markets.
choiceExplanations: The New Deal regulated but preserved private property and markets.
questions.distinguisher: The New Deal regulated banks rather than abolishing them.

questions.prompt: The famine in Ukraine in 1932 and 1933 was linked to
choices: Soviet policies that raised peasants' grain supplies
Soviet collectivization of agriculture
the American New Deal
the Treaty of Versailles
questions.explanation: Forced collectivization and grain seizures contributed to the famine.
choiceExplanations: Forced collectivization and grain seizures contributed to the famine.
The treaty did not cause the famine.
questions.distinguisher: Collectivization took grain from peasants; it did not raise their supplies.

questions.prompt: Countries that exported raw materials were hurt by the Depression mainly because
choices: they had no trade with industrial countries
the prices of their exports rose sharply
the prices of their exports fell sharply
demand for their goods rose too quickly
questions.explanation: Falling prices for goods such as coffee cut their income.
choiceExplanations: They depended on trade with industrial countries.
Falling prices for goods such as coffee cut their income.

questions.prompt: Which claim about responses to the Depression is most defensible?
choices: Governments of many kinds expanded their economic role
Every government returned to laissez-faire
Only democracies responded to the crisis
Governments reduced their economic role
questions.explanation: Democratic, communist, and fascist states all took on new economic roles.
choiceExplanations: Democratic, communist, and fascist states all took on new economic roles.
Soviet and fascist states also responded.
questions.distinguisher: Few governments relied on laissez-faire after 1929.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, by 1933 about what share of American workers was unemployed?
choices: Almost none
About one in four
About one in a hundred
About three in four
questions.explanation: About one in four workers was unemployed.
choiceExplanations: About one in four workers was unemployed.
The share was one in four.
questions.distinguisher: One in four, not three in four.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.4 key concept: following World War I and the Great Depression, governments took a more active role in economic life
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, summarizing the Great Depression, 1929–1939
stimulusBlocks.text:
In October 1929, stock prices in New York collapsed. Banks failed, factories closed, and the value of world trade shrank by about two-thirds over the next few years as countries raised tariffs to protect their own industries. By 1933, about one in four American workers was unemployed. Countries that exported raw materials, such as Brazil and its coffee growers, were hit hard as prices fell.

The crisis discredited the idea that markets would recover on their own. Governments everywhere experimented with new ways to manage their economies.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, the Depression spread internationally partly because
choices: countries lowered tariffs and trade grew
the United States ended all foreign trade
Brazil's coffee prices rose sharply as demand grew
countries raised tariffs and world trade shrank
questions.explanation: Rising tariffs helped cut the value of world trade by about two-thirds.
choiceExplanations: The value of world trade fell sharply, but trade continued.
Rising tariffs helped cut the value of world trade by about two-thirds.
questions.distinguisher: Prices fell, hurting exporters such as Brazil.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, the New Deal
choices: forced peasants onto collective farms
directed industry toward rearmament
created jobs and regulated banks while keeping markets
put the entire American economy under direct state control
questions.explanation: It created jobs, regulated banks, and kept private property.
choiceExplanations: It created jobs, regulated banks, and kept private property.
questions.distinguisher: Rearmament describes fascist Italy and Nazi Germany.

stimulusBlocks.source: CED Topic 7.4 key concept: governments responded to economic crisis with the New Deal, Soviet Five-Year Plans, and fascist corporatist economies
stimulusBlocks.attribution: Practice passage written for Page One, comparing government responses to economic crisis, 1928–1939
stimulusBlocks.text:
In the United States, Franklin Roosevelt's New Deal, begun in 1933, created public works jobs, regulated banks, and established Social Security, while keeping private property and markets. In the Soviet Union, Joseph Stalin's Five-Year Plans, begun in 1928, put the entire economy under state control, building heavy industry at great speed and forcing peasants onto collective farms. The collectivization of farms contributed to a famine in Ukraine in 1932 and 1933 that killed millions.

In fascist Italy and Nazi Germany, private companies remained, but the state directed industry toward national goals such as rearmament.

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, fascist economies differed from the Soviet economy in that fascist states
choices: abolished all private property
collectivized agriculture
left industry entirely to private owners without direction
kept private companies under state direction
questions.explanation: Private companies remained but served state goals.
choiceExplanations: Private companies remained but served state goals.
questions.distinguisher: Fascist states directed private firms; they did not leave them alone.
